subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Amazon Rainforest
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Amazon Rainforest.

hook.text: The Amazon covers 5.5 million square kilometers — larger than the entire European Union.

buildup.text: It holds 10% of all species on Earth and produces 6% of the world's oxygen.

discovery.text: The Amazon River discharges more water than the next seven largest rivers combined.

twist.text: Indigenous communities have managed these forests sustainably for over 10,000 years.

climax.text: Today the Amazon loses an area the size of a football field roughly every 30 seconds.

punchline.text: The world's greatest forest is shrinking in real time.

quiz.question: What share of Earth's species does the Amazon hold?

details.summary: The Amazon rainforest spans 5.5 million square kilometers across nine countries and contains roughly 10 percent of all species on Earth. It stores an estimated 150 to 200 billion tons of carbon and generates much of its own rainfall through transpiration.
details.whyItMatters: The Amazon is the planet's largest tropical forest and a global climate regulator. Its fate affects rainfall, biodiversity, and carbon cycles far beyond South America.
takeaways: The Amazon covers an area roughly half the size of Europe
It stores 150 to 200 billion tons of carbon in biomass and soil
Roughly 17 percent has been cleared, approaching a tipping-point threshold

faq.question: Why is the Amazon called the lungs of the Earth?
faq.answer: The Amazon produces massive amounts of oxygen through photosynthesis, though it also consumes most of it through respiration. Its real atmospheric importance is absorbing CO2 and regulating regional rainfall through transpiration of water vapor.

faq.question: Which countries share the Amazon rainforest?
faq.answer: Brazil holds about 60 percent, with significant portions in Peru, Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Bolivia, Guyana, Suriname, and French Guiana. Deforestation rates and protections vary widely among these countries.
